stemMd: All the winning entries in a design contest used recycled materials. The organizer concludes that using recycled materials guarantees a prize. The argument is flawed because it

options.label: A
options.textMd: draws a conclusion about all contests from several contests.

options.label: B
options.textMd: confuses the number of entries with their monetary value.

options.label: C
options.textMd: treats a feature shared by all winners as sufficient to win.

options.label: D
options.textMd: assumes that recycled materials are inexpensive.

options.label: E
options.textMd: rejects a claim solely because of its source.

explanationMd: The evidence says winners used recycled materials: winning implies recycled materials. The conclusion reverses that implication. Many losing entries might also have used recycled materials.

distractorRationale.b: Neither quantity nor value supplies the inference.
distractorRationale.d: No price claim appears in the reasoning.
distractorRationale.e: There is no attack on a speaker.
